description: This case study analyses how Manitoba, Canada, succeeded in siting a hazardous waste management facility when many other siting attempts had failed. Geoffrey Castle of the University of British Columbia published it in Air & Waste, the journal of the Air and Waste Management Association, in 1993. The paper describes the process that led to the siting success, including the volunteer site selection approach, and assesses the co-management agreement made between the proponent and the Rural Municipality of Montcalm, which gave the host community a role in overseeing safety and environmental quality. The analysis rests mainly on personal interviews with people directly involved in site selection, who reviewed earlier drafts, supported by secondary sources. The article is available online by subscription, and its abstract is free in OpenAlex. Coverage is one provincial siting process. Caveats: it is an early account written while the co-management structure was new, and it is qualitative. The author argues that most failed siting attempts are procedural, not technical failures and that volunteer siting can break siting deadlock. Simulation uses: process lessons and community acceptance conditions for scenarios that locate new waste treatment facilities. Related records: the EPA waste storage and staging site selection tool (model-epa-waste-storage-staging-site-selection-tool) supports technical siting screening.
